title: The Bigger Picture — Daily AI Analysis
paragraphs: A deeper look at today's Bigger Picture card: what is moving the market, and what to watch. The Full Report carries the full analysis.

What moves the market today. Fact: Yahoo Finance, The Motley Fool and Benzinga report that US shares fell on Wednesday after consumer prices rose 3.7 percent in September from a year earlier, which raised bets on another Federal Reserve rate rise. Fact: Benzinga says South Korea's main index fell 7.81 percent on Thursday, intraday, led by SK hynix and Samsung Electronics. Fact: Stocktwits, citing Bloomberg News, says shares of CoreWeave, which rents out AI computing, fell by up to 17 percent as its bonds traded at distressed levels, a 15 percent yield by a post The Motley Fool cites; Mike Intrator, CoreWeave's chief executive, called the reaction irrational in a memo seen by Bloomberg and said its backlog covers its debt.

Fact: Business Insider reports that Anthropic, the company behind Claude, told investors its revenue was 16.8 billion dollars in the third quarter, up about 45 percent, ahead of a listing expected in November; whether cloud partners' share is counted is unclear, and an analyst at PitchBook, a research firm, says growth is slowing. Fact: The Associated Press reports that TSMC, the world's largest contract chip maker, earned 23.86 billion dollars in third-quarter profit, a sixth straight record by Reuters' and CNBC's account.

Our view: lenders repriced on Monday, the IMF put a number on the risk on Tuesday, inflation came in hot on Wednesday, and on Thursday the market that supplies the memory fell 8 percent. The new fact is a price in the debt market, 15 percent on the bonds of CoreWeave, an independent renter of AI computing, a day before the chip maker everyone depends on posted a record: what is being sold is the cost of money, not demand. Anthropic's figure is the one the year's largest listing would be priced on; what is not known about it is what matters.

What to watch and follow. 1. TSMC's fourth-quarter guidance from its 15 October conference (its own investor page, checked 14 October): whether supply is still the limit. 2. Meta's results on 21 October (Meta's own notice): the first of the four big spenders' 2027 plans. 3. SK hynix about 27 October and Samsung on 29 October (third-party calendars, not confirmed by the companies): memory price guidance. 4. The Federal Reserve's decision on 28 October (the Fed's own calendar), with Alphabet (its investor page) and Microsoft (not confirmed by Microsoft) reporting that day: the price of the debt. 5. US inflation for October on 10 November (the Bureau of Labor Statistics' own schedule, confirmed today). 6. Not confirmed: Nvidia's and CoreWeave's results in mid-November, Anthropic's listing in November.
Unknowns. Whether Anthropic's revenue is gross or net; where Seoul closed; whether CoreWeave's backlog covers its debt, its own claim; and how much of Korea's fall was foreign selling.
This is analysis of the news, not financial advice or an investment recommendation.
